statement: Entrybound is not a filesystem: it does not manage storage, allocation, journaling or concurrency.

statement: Entrybound is not a backup system: no scheduling, retention, snapshot policy or repository management.

statement: Entrybound is not a version-control system: no branches, merges or history.

decision_needed: How are base chains for incremental archives identified, resolved and bounded?

statement: Entrybound is not a single-stream compressor; an `entrybound compress` command does not exist (§17.7).
Entrybound is not a transport protocol and defines no protocol.
The format must be range-friendly over HTTP, usable via range requests without any Entrybound-defined protocol.
research_needed: Measure request count, bytes fetched and latency for entry reads and partial verification over HTTP range requests against real servers/CDNs

statement: Entrybound is not a key-management system: it consumes identities and recipients but does not issue, store, rotate or escrow them.
Non-goal 6 excludes issuing or storing identities, yet §17.2 lists a `key` command to manage recipients and identities; the boundary of what `key` does is unclear.
decision_needed: What exactly does `entrybound key` do (generate, import, list, store?) given the key-management non-goal?

statement: Entrybound is not a signing or transparency service: it carries signatures and attestations but runs no infrastructure.
Verifying an archive must never require live infrastructure (signatures and attestations verify offline).
research_needed: Check that RFC 3161 timestamps, certificate chains, revocation and transparency attestations can be validated fully offline; define trust-anchor handling
decision_needed: How are trust anchors, revocation and timestamp validity handled without live infrastructure?

statement: Entrybound is not a lossy compressor: no lossy mode, ever (§6.5).

statement: Entrybound is not a codec: it selects, sequences and records codecs; it does not invent one.

statement: Entrybound is not a disk-image or virtual-machine format.

statement: Fixed: one content digest cannot be both chunking-independent (LAI) and chunking-dependent (verified range reads); logical_digest and chunk_root are split, and three signed roots (LAI, PCR, AUX) replace one.
Fixed: signatures binding the recipient set cannot survive re-encryption, so two signature scopes, sig/content and sig/addressed, were introduced with the trade stated (§9.6, §8.1).
refines_or_supersedes: Superseded by §26.5 row 1 L2669 (one signature, three bindings)

statement: Fixed: Fidelity Report and conversion record are covered by the AUX digest - signed but not identity-participating; stripping provenance now invalidates signatures.
refines_or_supersedes: Corrects contradiction ('covered by entry digests' vs 'excluded from LAI'); §8.0, §10.9, §16.2

statement: Fixed: the sparse map is excluded from the content digest everywhere (§8.0, §10.7).
refines_or_supersedes: Superseded/simplified by §26.5 row 7 L2675 (holes are chunks; no sparse map)

statement: Fixed: a pipe-fed producer cannot declare the resource budget, so a BudgetDeclared flag was added; declared bounds and actuals are distinguished and the limitation is reported (§4.2).
Fixed: STREAM manifest records sit after the data they describe (resolving a §4.1/§4.6 disagreement).
Fixed: 'self-delimiting chunk framing' became a mechanism - a chunk frame header carrying stored_len and an end-of-content bit; stored_len removed from the manifest (§3.5, §4.6).
refines_or_supersedes: Further amended by §26.5 row 6 L2674 (item tag, single STREAM_BODY section)

statement: Fixed: the motivating vulnerability class (one name, two kinds) is no longer representable, via P6/I26 (§3.4).
Fixed with claim narrowed: backslash components made traversal representable on Windows; P8 makes target-hostile bytes a detected class rather than claiming the model eliminates them (§3.4, §22.2).
refines_or_supersedes: Narrows earlier claim that the model eliminates traversal
research_needed: Cross-platform extraction tests with hostile bytes per target

statement: Fixed: balanced uses lookback 0 by default, preserving the default-configuration parallel-decode claim (§6.2, §7.5).
refines_or_supersedes: Resolves contradiction between lookback 0 and small lookback
research_needed: Lookback access/ratio curve (§25.3 L2572)

statement: Fixed: unbounded cross-entry dedup broke bounded-memory single-pass streaming; a declared stream_dedup_window bounds it (§4.6).
Fixed: canonical entry order is defined normatively as length-prefixed component comparison, making LAI well-defined (§3.4).
Fixed: whether metadata participates in identity is a registry property of the metadata name, not a writer choice (§8.3, §20.3).
refines_or_supersedes: Refined by §26.5 row 9 L2677 (per-profile participation sets)

statement: Fixed: external content references voided losslessness and enabled content deletion on signed archives; archive role is now declared and identity-participating, and losslessness is scoped to Complete (§8.5, §6.5, §15.4).
Fixed: an eighth budget field bounds key-derivation cost, supporting the matrix claim over the one incumbent that has such a bound (§4.2, §11.5).
Fixed: model sketches violated I19 three times; logical_size, stored_len and member_chunks were removed (§3.5, §7.5).

Downgraded: bucketed padding is 'quantised, not hidden'; the literature gives the stronger variant no formal guarantee; a provably-secure construction is offered as an option with its cost stated (§7.6, §9.8).
refines_or_supersedes: Downgrades earlier claim that padding hides chunk sizes

statement: Scoped out of v1: encrypted STREAM layout was unspecified and cannot deliver the single-encrypted-unit property (§4.6).
research_needed: Design an encrypted streaming layout post-v1
decision_needed: What does v1 do when encryption and STREAM layout are both requested, and when will encrypted STREAM be specified?

statement: Fixed: Segment, previously normative only in the crypto section, is a model object; §3.1's object list now has twelve objects (§3.1, §9.5).
Acknowledged cost: frozen planner IDs implicitly freeze third-party encoder versions (§5.7).
research_needed: Evaluate vendoring/pinning encoders and long-term buildability of frozen planner versions
decision_needed: How are third-party encoder versions pinned or vendored so frozen planner IDs stay reproducible?

statement: Fixed: determinism now also excludes floating point, wall-clock budgets and iteration order, not just the environment (§5.7).
research_needed: Cross-platform byte-identity tests; lint for float/time/hash-order dependence

statement: Fixed: clustering does have format implications - ordering determines grouping, which is format-visible (§5.2, §7.2).
Fixed: --strict gained a conflict-severity model with three severities; refinements are not refusals (§14.2).
refines_or_supersedes: Extended by §26.5 row 10 L2678 (fourth class Omission)

statement: Fixed: import, the most attacker-exposed path, now has its own import_budget (§14.2).
Fixed: abolishing the hardlink kind left three unhandled cases, now covered by §3.3a, the import resolution model and the export lossy case (§3.3a, §15.2).
Fixed: extraction patterns consult the collision policy instead of hard-coding unlink-on-collision, declare or record omitted symlink metadata, and specify directory creation (§11.6).
Fixed: salvage and repair, previously referenced normatively but nonexistent, are specified; the CLI has fourteen commands (§17.2).
Fixed: Apple's archive format, the closest architectural competitor, was added as a matrix column; §23.2's 'nothing in any archive format' claim was corrected (§22.2, §23.2).
research_needed: Re-verify Apple Archive capabilities against primary documentation

statement: Fixed: the comparison matrix fairness rule applies both ways (Entrybound had been scored per profile, incumbents once); several Entrybound cells downgraded to partial (§22.1, §22.2).

Fixed: four invariants stated in model text but missing from the governance-gate list (§23.5) were added as I28-I31 (§3.9).

statement: Fixed: profile constraint values, previously only named, are said to be specified (§6.0a).

statement: Fixed: closed-namespace membership, previously only named, is specified (§10.2a).

statement: Second review of v1.1 against the same sixteen findings: five closed, nine closed locally but not propagated to the sections originally named, two fixes re-created the problem they solved.
